Persian Sweets for Nowruz

Served at: Nowruz

Makes about 24 piecesPrep 30 minCook 15 min

Nowruz, the Persian New Year, is celebrated with a variety of traditional sweets that symbolize renewal and sweetness for the year ahead. These confections are often shared with family and guests as part of the festive Haft-Seen table.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (400 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 cup (240 ml) water
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 1/2 teaspoon rose water
  • 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, crushed
  • 1 cup (120 g) chopped pistachios or almonds
  • Cornstarch for dusting

Method

  1. Combine sugar, water, and lemon juice in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
  2. Stir until sugar dissolves, then bring the mixture to a boil without stirring.
  3. Add crushed saffron and reduce heat to low; simmer until the syrup reaches the soft ball stage (about 235°F or 113°C on a candy thermometer).
  4. Remove from heat and stir in rose water.
  5. Pour syrup onto a greased or parchment-lined tray and allow to cool slightly until it begins to set but is still pliable.
  6. Sprinkle chopped nuts evenly over the syrup and gently press them in.
  7. Once fully set, dust the surface with cornstarch and cut into small squares or diamonds.
  8. Allow pieces to dry for several hours before serving.

Tips

  • Use a candy thermometer for precise syrup temperature to achieve the perfect texture.
  • Substitute rose water with orange blossom water for a different floral note.
  • Store sweets in an airtight container at room temperature for up to one week.
